items.reason: The named pattern is absent and already gated, and the compounding half needs network. I read both workflows end to end: every `${{ … }}` in agent-dispatch.yml and autofix.yml sits on a `KEY: ${{ … }}` line under `env:`, `with:`, `if:` or `concurrency:` — never inside a `run:` body — and every shell use is a quoted `"$VAR"`, which is the prescribed remediation rather than the bug (agent-dispatch.yml:144-155 binds the issue title/body/comment as data; autofix.yml:138 binds the head ref). It is enforced, not merely true: `scripts/security/check-actions.mjs` implements a `run-injection` rule that is STRICTER than the finding — `TRUSTED_IN_RUN` (line 229) allowlists only runner/job/strategy/matrix and a fixed set of `github.*` scalars, so all of `github.event.*`, `steps.*.outputs.*`, `needs.*` and `secrets.*` are blocking inside a `run:` — plus `script-injection` (actions/github-script) and `untrusted-checkout` (pull_request_target / workflow_run) rules; it runs as `npm run security:actions` in ci.yml:162 on every push and pull_request, inside the `Node quality` job that .github/rulesets/main.json makes a REQUIRED status check. This is now the third Ascent cycle to open this row (see the f4eedd2e skip in the previous lane report); editing the workflows to satisfy the scanner would delete the hardening. The floating-tag half is real but offline-impossible: 9 refs float (.github/actions-pin-allowlist.json), each enumerated in a shrink-only ratchet, and resolving a tag to a SHA requires asking GitHub what it points at today — inventing one breaks the workflow. That work is already owned: `.github/workflows/pin-actions.yml` runs `security:actions --resolve` weekly on a runner and opens the PR, and .github/dependabot.yml:112 already tracks github-actions weekly (Dependabot rewrites a SHA pin plus its trailing `# vX.Y.Z` comment, so pinning survives its updates — it will not convert a tag pin to a SHA, which is exactly why pin-actions.yml exists). Permissions on both jobs are already per-job and used: agent-dispatch needs contents:write (push the branch) + issues:write (every outcome is said on the issue); autofix needs contents:write (commit) + pull-requests:write (`gh pr comment`).

The premise — 'nothing that fails when they slip' — is false here; the convention is enforced by a repo-owned gate rather than by commitlint, and adding a commitlint config would be a second, divergent vocabulary. `scripts/release/commit-msg.mjs` derives its accepted types from `SECTIONS` in `scripts/release/prepare.mjs`, the table the CHANGELOG is actually cut from, so the gate and the changelog generator cannot disagree; it runs in two places. Locally: `.githooks/commit-msg`, wired by `scripts/hooks/install.mjs` from the `prepare` npm script, with `hooks:check` blocking in ci.yml when a hook goes missing or points at a script that no longer exists. In CI, which is the answer to the 'bypassed hook' bullet: the `commit-convention` job (ci.yml:235-258) runs `commit-msg.mjs --base <PR base | HEAD~1> --head HEAD` over every commit in the pushed range, on both `push` and `pull_request`, and `Commit convention (subjects the changelog is cut from)` is a REQUIRED status check in .github/rulesets/main.json:31. A non-conforming subject fails that check; the only waiver is a `Commit-convention-exemption: <why>` trailer a reviewer can read in `git log`. The one live sub-question is the third bullet, and I could not close it honestly: `.claude/**` is ignored wholesale in eslint.config.mjs:13 because `.claude/worktrees/` holds full repo copies, and the boundary is now wrong in one place — `.claude/skills/motionize/tools/*.mjs` (8 files) is vendored, project-owned code that GENERATES committed source under app/_components/glyph/, and it is outside every lint guarantee. The fix is to narrow that ignore to `.claude/worktrees/**` (everything else under .claude is .md/.json, so nothing else would be newly linted), but `npm run lint` feeds the required `Node quality` check and this session has no shell to run eslint — shipping an unverified widening of a required gate could turn main red for everyone. A human should run: sed the ignore to `.claude/worktrees/**`, then `npm run lint`.

lessons: In this organization's repositories a maturity gap is answered with a repo-owned ratchet script, not a config file for a named tool: commit convention is scripts/release/commit-msg.mjs deriving its vocabulary from the changelog generator's own SECTIONS table, action pinning is scripts/security/check-actions.mjs over an enumerable shrink-only allowlist, ruff debt is scripts/lint/ruff-ratchet.mjs. Every one of them is wired into a REQUIRED status check in .github/rulesets/main.json and carries a written waiver trailer. Before opening a D6/D9 gap against one of these repos, read .github/rulesets/main.json and scripts/ — a scanner keyed on tool names (commitlint, husky) will report 'holds by habit' against a convention that is a required check.

A finding of 'untrusted input in a run step' can be raised by untrusted context bound into a step's `env:` — which is the documented FIX for script injection, not the bug. Verify by reading the `run:` bodies before touching a workflow. kp has now had THREE cycles open this same D9 row against two workflows that were already correct, already fixture-tested, and already gated by a rule stricter than the finding; each 'resolution' would have removed hardening. If a row survives two verified skips, the detector needs the fix, not the repository.

Pinning actions to SHAs, resolving digests, and reading CI history are the recurring offline-impossible asks in this lane. kp has already automated its half (pin-actions.yml runs `security:actions --resolve` weekly with a runner's network and token, and prunes the allowlist entries it burns down), so the honest lane outcome is a skip that names the weekly job — not a new workflow that duplicates it. Check for an existing scheduled burn-down before writing one.

The genuinely open guardrail gap in a mature agent-heavy repo is the harness itself: kp's eslint.config.mjs ignores `.claude/**` for a good reason (agent worktrees are full repo copies) and thereby also exempts vendored skill tooling that writes committed source. Closing that boundary needs a lint run, so a no-shell lane cannot do it — but it is worth raising as its own item, scoped to `.claude/worktrees/**`, in any repo whose skills directory holds real code rather than markdown.
